name: 70,000 Light-Years from Home
rationale: Cheap unconditional exile also answers dormant Spacecraft; giving a basic to hand is a real but modest drawback.

name: Andromedan Automatons
rationale: First copy can generate multiple cards; 3/1 body trades with Officer tokens so copies and artifact payoffs matter more than combat.

name: Antagonist Incorporator
rationale: Efficient defensive body and repeatable Borg production; evasion from Organic Avulsion Unit or Locutus turns contact into a growing board.

name: Assembly Specialist
rationale: Two artifact bodies for two mana enable affinity, sacrifice, team buffs and profitable beam-me-up replays.

name: Brad Boimler, Eager Ensign
rationale: Lifelink stabilizes early; station taps enable the counter replacement before charging ships or growing creatures.

name: Captain Benjamin Sisko
rationale: Two-drop produces bodies from modal spells and modal creature triggers; five-color activated ability is a rare late bonus.

name: Captain Jean-Luc Picard
rationale: Three-mana anthem plus a token for every creature or Spacecraft spell immediately snowballs; tutor is optional upside rather than necessary.
adjustment_reason: Three-mana anthem and a body plus tokens from both creature and ship casts is a more unconditional snowball than the typical high-grade historical engine; Agent Bishop and Mighty Mutanimals anchor the upper tail.

name: Command Decision
rationale: Cheap answer to large creatures and completed ships, with a cantrip floor that also triggers dilemma payoffs.

name: Command Subadjunct
rationale: Two-power artifact one-drop supports aggressive Borg decks; vigilance preserves blockers and station opportunities.

name: Conquest Mission
rationale: Three-mana setup recoups value with two nontoken artifacts; high artifact density supports it, but token artifacts do not trigger it.
adjustment_reason: Borg tokens can block and gain artifact-lord buffs; the set has many cheap nontoken artifacts, giving this setup enchantment better support than an unsupported engine.

name: Deanna Troi, Psychic Counsel
rationale: Efficient two-drop adds permanent stats to every subsequent creature and token; strong with go-wide plans and beam replays.

name: DOT-7 Repair Squad
rationale: Solid evasive artifact body; untap ability lets a creature station and still attack, or station two ships in one turn.

name: Dr. Beverly Crusher
rationale: No built-in lifegain, but each Medic, lifelink, Food or dual-land event adds two counters because Crusher doubles her own trigger; beam can repeat those events.

name: Dr. McCoy, Surly Surgeon
rationale: Initial body is small for four mana, but saves countered creatures repeatedly and pairs with distributed counters and Doctor EMH.

name: Emergency Medical Hologram
rationale: Can be a one-mana artifact 1/2 or place the counter on a better body; attractive beam fuel and counter enabler but low standalone impact.

name: Excalbian Gamemaster
rationale: Six-mana 6/6 adds multiple bodies immediately; death triggers distribute counters and turn chump blocks into lasting board strength.

name: Federation Field Medic
rationale: Often a four-mana vigilance body plus card, since any permanent counter qualifies; modal ETB is especially good to replay.

name: Federation Resupply
rationale: Selection rather than advantage on first cast; improves when tutoring a bomb ship and replaying a value creature, but consumes considerable mana.

name: Free Borg Revolutionaries
rationale: Landcycling prevents early dead draws; large artifact body and temporary team boost support go-wide attacks.

name: Ghost of Illyria
rationale: Efficient flyer with repeatable value when paired with beam recursion; blink reuses strong ETBs and resets problematic enchantments.

name: Hologram Janeway
rationale: Three-mana 3/3 artifact with a realistic eight-total-power payoff; Spacecraft eventually help meet the threshold.

name: Malfunctioning Holodeck
rationale: Three-mana Oblivion Ring with ward and artifact synergies; answers almost every bomb, including dormant ships and engines.

name: The Measure of a Man
rationale: Temporary exile is not permanent removal; can instead blink a friendly ETB creature, and the Clue provides eventual material.

name: Miles O'Brien, Transporter Ops
rationale: ETB can immediately draw at end step; repeated beam casts draw additional cards and the body is efficiently sized.

name: The Needs of the Many
rationale: Requires sacrificing a creature and leaving mana open; powerful team protection only when already developed, with little proactive value.

name: Oberth-Class Starship
rationale: Fixes the next land drop and supplies an artifact; six station counters are substantial for only a 2/2 flyer, so assess chiefly as a land finder.

name: Peace in Our Time
rationale: Opponent chooses whether to skip combat; four-mana symmetrical draw engine rarely reaches twelve counters before decisive combat or removal.

name: Pet Sehlat
rationale: Good three-mana power for station and eight-power attacks; needs a partner to attack and trades down into small blockers.

name: Picard, Leading by Example
rationale: Reusable power boost can improve combat or station output, but sorcery timing and tapping the source constrain defense and tempo.

name: Primary Unimatrix Adjunct
rationale: Borg double strike creates large immediate attacks with even modest artifact boards; fragile body and four-mana cost keep it below the best bombs.

name: Pure Energy
rationale: Counters spread efficiently and recur through beam; strong with lifelink and counter payoffs, but returning a creature is not free board development.

name: Rutherford, Upgraded Ensign
rationale: Six-card artifact selection is likely to replace itself in this environment; body and subsequent counters make a reliable value creature.

name: Saavik, Stoic Student
rationale: Flash creature usually removes an attacker using existing diverse types; five mana and Borg-heavy boards reduce consistency.

name: Set Phasers to . . .
rationale: One-mana defensive removal or proactive stun is flexible; targets an attacker for damage and cannot permanently kill larger creatures.

name: Shields Up!
rationale: Protection plus permanent counter wins combat and protects high-value engines; can also save a dormant Spacecraft.

name: Shuttle Ace
rationale: Five-mana evasive attacker stabilizes with lifegain; stationing also triggers the life, but cannot fly when blocking.

name: Sulu, Space Swashbuckler
rationale: First-strike two-drop with a conditional draw engine; sequencing equipment or ships before attacking or stationing makes the condition attainable.

name: Tactical Officer
rationale: Fragile early body; eight-power attack condition comes later, but accumulated counters and untapping help offensive boards.

name: Test of Conviction
rationale: Two-mana permanent team boost is excellent with Borg and Officer tokens; draw mode prevents dead hands but gives opponent a card.

name: There's Coffee in that Nebula
rationale: Selects land or a cheap permanent with high hit rate; beam provides late value and ETB reuse without being an immediate extra card.

name: Troubling Tribbles
rationale: Exponential 0/1 tokens cannot block and need a power anthem or sacrifice payoff; too much setup for an ordinary deck.

name: Una Chin-Riley, Number One
rationale: Durable five-drop makes attacks difficult to block after the eight-power threshold; no ETB value or independent evasion.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit
rationale: Three bodies immediately stabilize and charge the ship over two turns; ward plus a 5/5 flying lifelinker is a powerful endgame.
adjustment_reason: Three entry tokens both stabilize and support station; ward and flying lifelink greatly improve the payoff after charging.

name: U.S.S. Excelsior, Cutting Edge
rationale: Four-mana removal spell with a later 4/4 flyer attached; destroy target tapped creature can miss defensive engines and requires a legal target.

name: Vexing Drone
rationale: Efficient artifact body with useful tempo ETB; tap effect is especially valuable to replay when attacking with Borg.

name: Anthropological Mission
rationale: Noncreature spells include ships and artifacts; first two triggers filter, later triggers generate cards, but the setup costs a turn without a body.
adjustment_reason: Cheap artifacts, ships and beam spells supply more noncreature casts than ordinary creature-heavy pools; retain most of the historical setup penalty but partially offset it.

name: The Caretaker
rationale: Large vigilant ward body stabilizes; subsequent modal spells generate free opposing spells, including on opposing turns with instant dilemmas.

name: Cetacean Ops
rationale: Ward protects a body that permanently grows with noncreature casts; strong if deployed before the spell-heavy turns, slower than cheap threats.

name: Cloak and Phaser
rationale: Usually costs five or six rather than nine; two bodies plus net card advantage are substantial, but unique-land requirements delay it.

name: Cloistered Telepath
rationale: Flash two-drop trades while filtering a card; excellent replay target for beam and helps fill the graveyard.

name: Consider the Prime Directive
rationale: Soft counter remains useful because the other mode replaces itself and buys a combat step; reliably triggers dilemma abilities.

name: Data, New Life
rationale: Starts vulnerable but naturally grows each draw step and scales sharply with draw-two spells and beam cantrips.

name: Deep Space Scan
rationale: Six-mana draw-only spell needs several unique land names to outperform cheaper draw spells and adds no board presence.

name: Dominion Saboteur
rationale: Copies best artifact or creature with counters intact and removes legendary restriction; can copy an already-stationed ship or either player's bomb.

name: Emergency Holographic Crew
rationale: Good defensive stats and modal ETB; either recovers a ship or fills the graveyard and sets up draws, with profitable beam replays.

name: Energize
rationale: Cheap tempo and a second cast; sorcery timing and opponent ETB creatures constrain it, while returning your own creature can create value.

name: Ensign Pavel Chekov
rationale: Defensive body usually finds a playable opposing land among several cards; no extra land drop, and off-color lands mostly support unique names.

name: Enterprise NX-01
rationale: ETB delays an attacker before becoming an evasive vigilant threat; station six still requires real creature taps.

name: Federation Probe
rationale: Cheap flying artifact with modal ETB; enables dilemma and artifact engines and is easy to beam, though the unassisted body is small.

name: Guidance Failure
rationale: Instant broadly answers creatures or dormant ships; cheaper against attackers, but top-library option gives opponent a redraw.

name: Gwyndala, the Progeny
rationale: Baseline two-mana 2/2 leaves Equipment after removal; token-copy ability is situational and still requires paying equip costs.

name: Highly Illogical
rationale: Four-mana hard counter with occasional two-mana use; holding up four is costly against value creatures and cheap spell chains.

name: H.M.S. Bounty, Unlikely Timeship
rationale: Whale tutor has common targets and gives immediate value; draw and extra-turn payoffs require charging eight counters and connecting.

name: Hoshi Sato, Exolinguist
rationale: Five-mana 3/3 usually finds one card from a useful selection; counts her own two types, but Borg boards reduce selection depth.

name: Humpback Whales
rationale: Landcycling keeps it useful early; large vigilant ward body defends well but lacks evasion and immediate card advantage.

name: Interstellar Effigy
rationale: Bounce attached to four power is useful tempo and a good beam target; five-mana cost and opposing ETBs limit repeated bouncing.

name: Jett Reno, Problem Solver
rationale: Repeated modal creature triggers grow Jett; station provides safe surveils and eventually draws once power reaches four.

name: Kobayashi Maru Scenario
rationale: Fourth upkeep forces losing the game; needs a fast win or a specific blink or sacrifice outlet, so nominal draw and token value overstates reliability.

name: Lieutenant Commander Data
rationale: Both players' noncreature spells grow Data; surplus counters become cheap cards, with counter removal available from all friendly creatures.

name: Lt. Cmdr. Geordi La Forge
rationale: Three power supports station even without text; doubling charge counters accelerates Spacecraft significantly but requires a supporting board.

name: Make It So
rationale: Four-mana draw two plus Officer is reliable material and dilemma support; untap mode occasionally completes a ship or generates mana instead.

name: Marooned
rationale: Cheap disabling Aura can wait for a creature to tap; paying four taps immediately, and beam prevention closes a major escape route.

name: Melkotian Adjudicator
rationale: Flying vigilance threat grows with each dilemma, including modal ETB creatures; three mana and one initial toughness expose it to cheap removal.

name: Mr. Spock, Science Officer
rationale: Doubles every draw, including routine draw steps and draw-two spells; four-toughness body survives small damage and the advantage snowballs rapidly.
adjustment_reason: Doubles every draw on a four-toughness creature; historical Jace Beleren's repeatable card advantage anchors a stronger upper tail than the linear text model.

name: Nyota Uhura, Communications
rationale: Three-mana 2/4 is an effective blocker; choosing a common mana value generates extra cards as opponent develops, though late deployment is worse.

name: Open Communications
rationale: Cheap spell for noncreature engines and a later beam cast; returning a value creature is useful but must be repaid in mana and tempo.

name: Romulan Bird-of-Prey
rationale: Low initial cost with hexproof while dormant; noncreature casts help reach eight counters without forfeiting all creature attacks.

name: Rules of Acquisition
rationale: Steal mode gives opponent three cards; gifting a disposable token for draw three is often better, but five-mana timing and material costs matter.

name: Scotty, Miracle Worker
rationale: Reuses instant and sorcery cards at normal mana cost while returning ETB creatures; main-phase restriction prevents instant-speed protection loops.

name: Seven of Nine, Unassimilated
rationale: Two-mana 0/4 blocks while looting every turn; five unique lands eventually unlock extra cards, while the seven-name transformation is a remote bonus.

name: Starfleet Spanner Jockey
rationale: Efficient defensive body and three station power; noncreature-heavy decks can attack often, but it cannot attack without casting a spell first.

name: Subcommander T'Pol
rationale: Flash body with modal stun gives flexible tempo and dilemma triggers; Stifle mode is narrower than countering a spell.

name: Suurok-Class Science Vessel
rationale: Immediate card replaces the investment; five station counters are relatively attainable for a 3/2 flyer and artifact ETB synergies add value.

name: Suus Mahna Practitioner
rationale: Three-power creature becomes a reasonably cheap repeatable tapper once three or four distinct lands are established.

name: Test of Priorities
rationale: Selection cantrip is a useful floor and delayed blink protects or reuses creatures; only one mode is chosen, so protection does not also draw.

name: Those Old Scientists
rationale: Looting fills the graveyard for beam, then chapter two recovers a useful card; third chapter adds little immediate material.

name: V'Ger, the Intruder
rationale: Seven-mana flyer replaces itself on entry and keeps drawing or weakens attackers; expensive without cycling but closes stalled games.

name: Vulcan Mind-Meld
rationale: One mana grants two persistent opposing cards with mana flexibility while giving opponent one of yours; no short play deadline, but symmetrical resources matter.

name: Wesley Crusher, Starfleet Cadet
rationale: Flash 2/2 chooses two useful effects; bounce is restricted to mana value two or less and the draw mode is filtering rather than advantage.

name: Zefram Cochrane, Warp Pioneer
rationale: Can generate extra artifact cards from the library top and gives every ship two counters; benefits from high artifact density without needing a ship immediately.

name: Armus, Skin of Evil
rationale: Discard mode is instant-speed three-mana -4/-4; late 6/6 menace strips hands every end step, giving useful early and late halves.

name: Assault Drone
rationale: Artifact lord improves its own power and wide Borg boards; four mana for a defensive 3/4 is fair but not a value play.

name: Automated Warfare System
rationale: Three-mana flyer converts disposable artifacts or creatures into cards on attack; Food, Borg tokens and exhausted value artifacts supply fodder.

name: Bat'leth
rationale: ETB kills small engines or blockers and leaves a reusable power boost; misses four-toughness creatures and costs mana to equip later.

name: Battle-Scarred Survivalist
rationale: Menace threat grows from either player's creature deaths, once each turn; token exchanges and sacrifice make growth consistent after the weak initial turn.

name: Blastoneuron
rationale: Flying body can reuse a cheap creature ETB immediately and gains drain from graveyard departures; requires a suitable graveyard target for full value.

name: Cha'DIch Investigator
rationale: Six power across two bodies for five mana, including a hasty token; valuable with Klingon sacrifice and excellent to replay through beam.

name: Collation Trimatrix
rationale: Cheap artifact body enables card drawing by tapping three artifact creatures; competes with station and attacks but works with summoning-sick tokens.

name: Collective Drone
rationale: Low-cost Borg scales in power with the artifact-creature board, both attacking and charging ships; two toughness remains vulnerable.

name: Commander Raffi Musiker
rationale: Three-mana 3/2 with either a Clue or graveyard interaction; repeated modal ETBs support dilemmas and beam value.

name: D'Ghor Bloodletter
rationale: Modal ETB either sweeps tokens or edicts; sacrifice mode is symmetrical but can sacrifice itself, and opponents can exploit expendable tokens.

name: Death Is Irrelevant
rationale: Eight-mana engine immediately reanimates at end step and gives Borg indestructible; very strong when cast but often stranded before then.

name: The Destruction of Praxis
rationale: Five-mana scalable sweeper normally clears small and medium creatures; six unique names for bonus tokens is uncommon.

name: De-evolve
rationale: Usually neutralizes an attacker and removes blocking immediately; artifact or creature activated engines remain functional until threshold exile.

name: Eject the Warp Core
rationale: Two-mana instant kills small creatures, or sacrifices a cheap artifact to kill almost any large creature; abundant expendable material supports kicker.

name: Elim Garak, Simple Tailor
rationale: Efficient menace 3/3 plus repeatable four-point life swings from modal spells and creature abilities; threatens quick wins while stabilizing.
adjustment_reason: Tal Shiar Operative and modal ETB creatures repeatedly trigger four-point life swings without spending another card on every trigger.

name: Fugitive Listener
rationale: Early discard is real card advantage and can be repeated via beam; three-power one-toughness body trades down against tokens.

name: Gabriel Lorca, Mirror Menace
rationale: Large menace threat returns cheaply from graveyard after a dilemma, making ordinary trades favorable; five-mana replay cost still matters.

name: General Chang, Cold Warrior
rationale: One-mana sacrifice outlet grows every Klingon permanently, including itself; token Klingons and multiple cheap Warriors create explosive combat.

name: Georgiou, Terran Emperor
rationale: Six-mana durable blocker draws at each end step and prevents life-total losses while alive; removing it at negative life is a serious vulnerability.

name: A Good Day to Die
rationale: Cheap power trick replaces itself only if the target dies; cannot save a creature and is awkward against exile, bounce or noncombat engines.

name: Grand Nagus Zek
rationale: Accumulates Treasures on either player's creature deaths and grows from them; starts small but supports ramp, splashes and sacrifice decks.

name: Gul Dukat, Colonial Prefect
rationale: Seven-mana menace bomb doubles opposing life loss each end step and gains that life; triple black and no reliable entry removal limit consistency.

name: He's Dead, Jim
rationale: Unconditional instant removal with surveil is reliable; four mana is less efficient than the best two-mana answers.

name: Hive Mind Coprocessor
rationale: A sturdy artifact body grants card draw to the whole Borg board on contact; menace and token swarms turn it into substantial advantage.

name: Impossible Choice
rationale: Instant draw two is a solid floor; removal creates two opposing tokens, so best used on bombs rather than routine creatures.

name: In the Pale Moonlight
rationale: Nontoken edict, Clue and later two bodies supply sustained material; five-mana initial investment can be punished by wide boards.

name: Kai Winn, Faithless Leader
rationale: Three-power two-drop is serviceable but one toughness trades poorly; blind naming rarely shuts off the opponent's most relevant card.

name: Khan, Vengeful Heart
rationale: Four-mana five-power body turns a disposable artifact or token into two cards immediately; casting from exile is useful additional resilience.

name: Obsidian Order Operative
rationale: Five toughness stalls ground attacks and modal chains drain repeatedly; low power and four-mana cost make it a defensive synergy piece.

name: Organic Avulsion Unit
rationale: Efficient artifact body and repeatable team menace; creates attacks for Borg card-draw and token-generation lords.

name: Overflow Submatrix
rationale: Efficient Borg body repeatedly recasts artifact creatures from the graveyard; finality limits infinite recycling but each recovery is valuable.

name: Pattern Buffer Preservation
rationale: Selection, self-mill and a cheap second cast; gains value with ETB creatures and graveyard payoffs but first casting does not add cards.

name: Relentless Drednok
rationale: Small lifelink artifact can trade or be sacrificed and later replaces itself; weak damage output and three-mana graveyard draw keep it modest.

name: Resistance Is Futile
rationale: Two-mana kill spell misses many Borg and other artifact creatures, but reanimation mode supplies a good alternative in artifact-heavy matchups.

name: Rogue Artificial Intelligence
rationale: Landcycling fixes early hands; large artifact body either stabilizes life or filters the next draws, with a modal trigger on entry.

name: Salt Vampire
rationale: Efficient lifelink two-drop disrupts a specific opposing card but replaces it; knowledge and lifegain matter more than raw card advantage.

name: Sela, Tal Shiar Paradox
rationale: First attack can immediately create a 2/2 if your own graveyard has a card; beam, cycling and graveyard activations provide additional token triggers.

name: Storied Veteran
rationale: Aggressive one-drop returns once through finality; supports Klingons and sacrifice but cannot stabilize by blocking.

name: Stray from History
rationale: Three-mana two-card recursion is useful after trades; hand-exile mode gives an early use and both modes trigger dilemmas.

name: Tal Shiar Operative
rationale: Attack trigger faces a dilemma every turn and can grant deathtouch to itself or another attacker; excellent support for repeated modal payoffs.

name: Tell Me What You See
rationale: Opponent controls the initial outcome and replay costs mana; repeated drain can matter with dilemmas but it adds no board and can be denied cards.

name: Tenacious Drone
rationale: Two artifact bodies across a death trigger for two mana; ideal for Borg lords, sacrifice, affinity and graveyard recasting.

name: Test of Loyalty
rationale: One-mana modal cantrip or creature recovery; cheap dilemma enabler with a decent late-game floor but no inherent card advantage.

name: U.S.S. Reliant, From Hell's Heart
rationale: Four-mana reanimation provides immediate value and the returned creature helps charge the ship; ten counters delay the recurring attack payoff.

name: Vengeance Mission
rationale: Every creature death drains but three-mana setup does not affect the board; relies on sustained exchanges or a sacrifice engine.

name: Academy Instructor
rationale: Noncreature casts produce permanent Officers and grow the Instructor's power; ships and reusable beam spells make repeated triggers realistic.

name: Beckett Mariner, Impetuous Ensign
rationale: First strike makes a useful aggressive two-drop; tapping for station also builds toward the occasional two-damage trigger.

name: Boarding Action
rationale: Hasty Klingon token contributes to sacrifice and tribal plans; beam provides a later body and value-creature replay at a tempo cost.

name: Brazen Bluff
rationale: Opponent can decline the exile when your free spell is weak or unavailable; double red and noncreature restriction make this unreliable interaction.

name: Cantankerous Captain
rationale: Reasonable defensive stats and a recurring power boost; eight-total-power condition later makes a key attacker harder to block.

name: Captain James T. Kirk
rationale: Immediate modal token or filtering and repeated attack triggers generate advantage; empty-hand mode selection turns it into a powerful army engine.

name: Captain Michael Burnham
rationale: Efficient trample body supplies damage on normal land drops; ramp and fetch effects add counters with second landfall triggers.

name: Captain's Tutelage
rationale: Flash first strike can win one combat, but the Aura remains exposed to two-for-one removal and supplies no toughness thereafter.

name: D-7 Battle Cruiser
rationale: Three station power turns this cheap ship into a free hasty Klingon each combat; those tokens can later help charge it or be sacrificed.
adjustment_reason: Only three counters unlock repeatable Klingons and several common or uncommon sacrifice payoffs turn the temporary tokens into lasting material.

name: Dahar Master
rationale: Four-power body can sacrifice an exhausted artifact, spare token or enchantment for two damage to any target; profitable ETB replay target.

name: Dominion Infiltration
rationale: Temporary copies can exploit ETBs or finish games, but triple red and dependence on opposing creatures make the card inconsistent.

name: Encounter the Unknown
rationale: Instant draw-two impulse gives a floor while two damage to all creatures can sweep tokens; double red and symmetrical damage require care.

name: Erica Ortegas, Plucky Pilot
rationale: Hasty body repeatedly produces extra landfall triggers and temporary mana; returned land can be replayed, but natural land drops are still required.

name: Exploratory Mission
rationale: Recurring landfall selection has a high ceiling; four-mana setup and same-turn play permission often waste the first revealed spell.

name: Genesis Effect
rationale: Six damage answers most creatures; replacing your land with New Planet can improve fixing, distinct names and landfall, but five mana is slow.

name: Horta
rationale: Large trampling finisher with an early landcycling option; lacks entry value, protection or immediate haste.

name: Infinite Diversity
rationale: Nine mana plus a graveyard spell and a diverse surviving board is excessive setup; poor when behind or drawn early.
adjustment_reason: Nine-mana spell also requires a graveyard spell and a surviving diverse board, producing correlated failure cases.

name: Khaaaaaaaaaaaannn!
rationale: Scalable instant removal efficiently kills four-toughness creatures for three mana and exiles recursion targets; cannot damage players.

name: Khan, Despot by Design
rationale: Five-power trample body immediately clears Officer and Borg tokens and small engines while leaving your own board intact.

name: La'An Noonien-Singh, Security
rationale: Good power and useful attack payoff, but requires eight total power and has no protective or card-advantage ETB.

name: Lwaxana Troi, Charming Guest
rationale: Efficient basic body; doubling another creature's future triggers costs two mana and removes this creature from attacks or station.

name: Munitions Enthusiast
rationale: Three-power trampler for two mana trades up and leaves a one-damage trigger that can finish another creature or hit a player.

name: The Naked Time
rationale: Temporary ramp must be used on a narrow chapter-two window, and chapter three sacrifices a land; poor lasting material without specific sequencing.

name: Pah-Wraith
rationale: Haste and first strike combine with immediate team power boost to threaten lethal; seven mana requires a deck able to reach its finishing turn.

name: Perils of the Past
rationale: Instant artifact destruction hits Borg, ships and engines; substantial pump mode provides a broadly useful alternative and a dilemma trigger.

name: Planetary Bombardment
rationale: One-mana removal is efficient against small creatures and tokens; four-damage upgrade requires a prior death and is not always available.

name: Planetary Patrol
rationale: Usually attacks as a three-power two-drop while land drops continue; lacks lasting growth or entry value.

name: Plasma Cascade
rationale: Instant three damage to any target with optional filtering; handles engines, finishes combat and turns surplus lands into new cards.

name: Q, Stacking the Deck
rationale: Four-mana 4/4 offers persistent replacement of bad hand cards with one sampled spell; copies still require paying mana and consume a card from hand.

name: Quark, Humble Proprietor
rationale: Treasure tokens cannot be sacrificed while Quark remains; bounce can eventually unlock stored mana, but the small body and unsupported tokens are poor alone.

name: Ravenous Cosmozoan
rationale: Graveyard spells reduce cost of a flying hasty threat; beam exiles its own spells, so discount should not assume every cast remains in the graveyard.

name: Reckless Impulse
rationale: Cheap two-card access supports noncreature engines and land drops; delayed permission helps use both cards, but it adds no immediate blocker.

name: Red Alert!
rationale: Team power boost can finish wide boards or trade up while blocking; defensive discount does not add toughness or save creatures.

name: Sarcophagus, Ship of the Dead
rationale: Immediate team power anthem supports tokens and eight-power attacks; ten-counter flying body arrives later, aided by creature deaths.

name: Savvy Profiteer
rationale: Two-mana creature ramps into four-drops and banks Treasure later; one toughness is fragile and mana is only red until Treasure production.

name: Silicate Surveyor
rationale: Four-power reach body plus a card playable through next turn is reliable top-end material, but five mana competes with stronger ships and bombs.

name: Starfleet Security
rationale: Cheap haste body can generate a Clue when it dies during your turn; small stats and conditional replacement make it primarily support material.

name: Tal Shiar Analyst
rationale: Three power can station efficiently and untaps after noncreature spells; repeated pings pressure life totals but cannot remove creatures.

name: Targ Wrangler
rationale: Five-power menace is an excellent rate until attacking requires repeated nonland sacrifices; disposable material helps but ongoing card loss is substantial.

name: Tasha Yar, Out of Time
rationale: Hasty two-drop replaces itself on death with temporary card access, then repeats once from the graveyard; strong sacrifice and graveyard-leaving synergy.

name: Test of Identity
rationale: Klingon double strike is a strong trick in the right deck; instant rummage-draw mode supplies a fallback and dilemma trigger.

name: Transporter Malfunction
rationale: Two-mana three damage to any target is strong initially; expensive triple-red beam is later value rather than the main reason to draft it.

name: Will Riker, First in the Field
rationale: Four-power body generates two temporary lands every combat, including entry turn; ramp, landfall and thinning all matter despite sacrificing those lands later.

name: Worf, Intelligence Contractor
rationale: Three-power body plus temporary theft of a cheap opposing creature enables a large attack; free sacrifice outlets can turn theft into permanent removal.

name: The Wrath of Khan
rationale: Three-mana four-damage removal with later filtering and a permanent edict; surviving larger creatures can instead be stolen for combat.

name: Adversary by Algorithm
rationale: Reasonable three-mana artifact body generated by a noncreature spell; beam adds a second body and can reuse an ETB creature.

name: Amok Time
rationale: Fight is conditional but followed by life and creature recovery; three chapters provide value when you can safely win the initial fight.

name: Astute Terraformer
rationale: Ordinary two-drop becomes a four-power creature at a reasonable activation cost as unique names accumulate; once-per-turn restriction prevents an unlimited pump sink.

name: Branching Timeline
rationale: Eight mana usually yields several tapped permanents but often includes lands; unique-name and high-cost requirements leave many early dead draws.

name: Captain Jonathan Archer
rationale: Three mana supplies four power across two bodies and three creature types; repeatable federation boost supports attacks and station acceleration.

name: Captain Kathryn Janeway
rationale: Explores immediately and for every subsequent creature, improving draws or adding counters; additional land play converts explored lands into tempo.
adjustment_reason: Self-explore and exploration on all future creatures support both counters and extra land plays; the initial effect and ongoing engine are unusually reliable.

name: Captain Pike, Fullness of Time
rationale: Power grows with unique lands and playing lands off the library provides real card advantage; double green and early two-basic-land boards constrain initial size.

name: Cold-Blooded Crew
rationale: Cycling solves early hands; entry counters create substantial stats or improve an existing threat, and small creatures cannot block it.

name: Common Goal
rationale: Two-mana combined bite can use two friendly creatures to kill a large target without fighting; needs a developed board and can be disrupted.

name: Culber and Stamets, Star-Crossed
rationale: Normally a four-mana 4/5 with a modal trigger; mana mode enables another spell or a splash while leaving a solid body.

name: Dathon and Picard at El-Adrel
rationale: Pump mode is useful, but three mana is expensive and opposing artifact/enchantment edict cannot reliably hit a chosen bomb amid spare artifacts.

name: David and Carol Marcus, Creators
rationale: Defensive body plus a permanent land token ramps and fixes all colors; excellent to replay through beam, though repeated tokens share one name.

name: Dominion Assault Force
rationale: Vigilant 4/4 gives useful station power without sacrificing future blocks; modal surveil or graveyard interaction adds flexibility and dilemma triggers.

name: Dominion Supervisor
rationale: Can be a three-mana 4/2 or improve a better creature; trample for countered creatures helps distribute counters and push damage.

name: Dr. Joseph M'Benga
rationale: Doubles creature counters and protects other countered creatures; strong with Doctors, dilemma growth and landfall, but does not protect itself by default.

name: Dr. Leonard "Bones" McCoy
rationale: Flash body returns a non-Doctor permanent or insures another creature against death; non-Doctor restriction matters but artifact and creature targets are plentiful.

name: Final Frontier
rationale: Three-mana ramp finds dual-color Planets as well as basics; cheap beam can ramp again and reuse a creature, at the cost of rebuilding that body.

name: First Contact
rationale: Instant selection almost always finds a permanent and fills the graveyard; useful consistency rather than raw advantage, with first-spell life a small bonus.

name: Genesis Device
rationale: Permanent ramp also counts as an artifact; expensive later activation converts basic lands into utility lands and extra unique names rather than adding land count.

name: Holo-Engineer
rationale: Four mana immediately supplies two 3/3s, then turns Officer, Borg, Food, Clue and even Planet tokens into 3/3 artifacts; token utility is lost but board power is enormous.
adjustment_reason: Immediate six power for four mana and common token-producing creatures support the replacement effect without additional rare cards.

name: Hologram Stalker
rationale: Returning a permanent immediately triggers a 3/3 token as well as the 2/2 body; later beam and graveyard departures generate more tokens once each turn.

name: I'm a Doctor, Not a . . .
rationale: One-mana trick untaps and supplies a temporary +1/+1 plus permanent counter; supports counter engines and station while remaining combat-efficient.

name: Jadzia Dax, Living Legacy
rationale: Two-mana creature grows and produces increasing green mana every first main phase; provides both early acceleration and a scaling body without tapping.
adjustment_reason: Counter growth, non-tapping acceleration and a scaling body combine in one cheap card, with multiple large payoffs in the supplied set.

name: Jake Sisko, War Correspondent
rationale: Efficient body gains life from normal land drops and Clues from second landfalls; ramp, Anomalies and temporary land engines improve the draw rate.

name: MACO Strike Team
rationale: Aggressive one-drop replaces targeted removal or combat tricks with an Officer; opponent can still block it and tokens enter tapped.

name: Moopsy
rationale: Cheap deathtouch creature discourages large attackers and can gain reach against ships; weak station power and susceptibility to pings limit it.

name: Mugato
rationale: Five-mana 6/6 with reach, vigilance and deathtouch dominates many combats and provides station power; no entry card advantage or protection.

name: Neelix, Moral Support
rationale: Food supplies one reliable growth trigger and later lifegain can grow it further; starts as a low-impact 1/1 and needs mana or supporting cards.

name: Photosynthetic Physician
rationale: Five-power reach body stabilizes against flyers and charges ships; graveyard token adds value after trading or being milled.

name: Rok-Tahk, Budding Scientist
rationale: Six mana provides a 5/5 and indestructible chump blocker; team mana arrives late, so do not value it like an early mana engine.

name: Saru, Unthreatened
rationale: Flash body can save a valuable creature from targeted removal while improving the board; no protection from sweepers or combat damage.

name: Saurian Explorer
rationale: Four-power body attacks larger on landfall and supplies a repeatable late land-token sink; no immediate value if unable to attack.

name: Species 8472
rationale: Large body gains several life and bypasses Borg blockers; six mana and vulnerability to nonartifact removal limit the tribal protection.

name: Stable Wormhole
rationale: Each attack ramps permanently into any color and triggers landfall; three-mana setup adds no blocker and repeated New Planets do not add unique names.

name: Support Mission
rationale: Every later creature receives permanent stats and eventually two counters; slow initial investment but especially effective with repeated creature tokens.

name: Sylvia Tilly, Joy of Discovery
rationale: ETB surveil stocks beam spells and graveyard fuel; recurring combat counter costs only one mana and can immediately improve a creature on later turns.

name: Syndicate Liquidators
rationale: Landfall distributes two permanent counters each turn, creating a rapidly growing team; five-mana initial 4/4 needs a land drop to supply immediate extra value.

name: Temporal Conqueror
rationale: Three-mana defensive body replaces itself with a land or Treasure after milling; supports graveyard engines, splashes and beam ETB reuse.

name: Test of Courage
rationale: Very cheap artifact/enchantment answer hits many early engines and Borg but misses large ships; graveyard-exile lifegain mode is a weak fallback.

name: U.S.S. Discovery, at Black Alert
rationale: Five mana immediately discovers a real spell and later attacks repeat it; six station counters are attainable and the final body is evasive.
adjustment_reason: Discover 5 provides a real spell on entry and on later attacks; station six is supported by green bodies, distinguishing it from ships with no entry material.

name: U.S.S. Voyager, Lone Wanderer
rationale: Four-mana double land ramp is substantial and later leaves a flying vigilance ship; eight counters require another board, and entry does not block immediately.

name: Warp Speed
rationale: Replaces itself with a land but does not ramp on entry; untapped lands help the many taplands, while the eventual draw activation still needs blue mana.

name: Xenobotanist
rationale: Two-mana any-color source has three toughness and ramps into powerful four-drops; supports splashes without needing extra off-color lands.

name: Xindi Surveyors
rationale: Three-mana body receives permanent counters on ordinary land drops; extra landfall can quickly turn it into a large threat and station resource.

name: All Good Things...
rationale: Three draw-two/exile-one chapters generate sustained selection and material, with possible life at the end; five mana in two colors adds no immediate blocker.

name: Borg Cube
rationale: Affinity makes entry exile affordable in a Borg deck; later attacks assimilate the exiled creature and twelve counters grant team evasion, but charging still takes a board.
adjustment_reason: Common double-body artifact creatures make affinity relevant, while entry exile supplies value before station twelve is reached.

name: The City on the Edge of Forever
rationale: Phases out both boards and uses a fragile token to lock phasing; draw and life buy time, but ending the lock can return opposing creatures before yours.

name: Cleveland Booker, Empath
rationale: Hybrid landfall engine makes a 2/2 on every land drop; tokens cannot block, so it is stronger offensively and with sacrifice or repeated land entry.

name: Constable Odo
rationale: Hybrid five-drop has an immediate modal ETB: two Clues for material or two stun counters for tempo; strong beam target but expensive.

name: Dal R'El, Augment Orphan
rationale: Efficient gold body generates temporary mana from landfall and later turns surplus lands into cards; sacrificing lands can undo unique-name thresholds.

name: Daniels, Temporal Agent
rationale: Hybrid Gravedigger is broadly castable and synergizes with beam; graveyard activation supplies life and a departure trigger after death or self-mill.

name: Dathon, His Heart Open
rationale: Three distinct colors and limited enchantment density constrain the draw engine; Saga-counter activation is useful but cannot justify unsupported casting demands.

name: The Doctor, EMH
rationale: Hybrid five-drop is at least a 5/5 when targeting itself and distributes extra counters to the existing countered team; excellent with repeated ETBs.

name: The Duras Sisters
rationale: Two hybrid mana supplies a 3/2 followed by a hasty 2/1 when it dies; excellent Klingon fodder with strong standalone material.

name: D'Vana Tendi, Optimistic Ensign
rationale: Sturdy hybrid three-drop can untap a mana source, attacker, tap engine or station contributor; surveil is an additional late sink rather than immediate draw.

name: Gowron, Eager for Battle
rationale: Free sacrifice outlet grows from all creature deaths; sacrificing Klingons also draws cards, with multiple repeatable Klingon-token sources available.

name: Gray and Adira, Forever Joined
rationale: Hybrid engine copies a creature each combat after a noncreature cast, reusing ETBs and adding a hasty attacker; requires a creature board and spell sequencing.

name: Hemmer, Fixing What Is Broken
rationale: Efficient gold body loots when attacking or stationing; ship hexproof applies only during your turn, so it does not prevent all opposing removal.

name: Hit It!
rationale: Ramp and team haste combine well with large creatures and landfall; no creature body and three-color-style gold demand keep the floor moderate.

name: The Inner Light
rationale: Reanimates a green or white creature immediately, then offers a large combat-draw opportunity; needs a suitable graveyard and a way to connect.

name: Kira Nerys, Firebrand
rationale: Efficient trampling gold attacker boosts later creatures and turns combat-time tokens into attackers; lacks an immediate token or card itself.

name: Kirk, Commanding Officer
rationale: Gold 3/3 supplies attack-card access at eight total power, and a sacrifice option answers artifacts or enchantments; must establish a board to draw reliably.

name: Live Long and Prosper
rationale: Seven mana can gain substantial life, but draw scales with cards left in hand and no blocker is created; often too little material when expensive hands finally empty.

name: Locutus, the One Who Speaks
rationale: Two-mana Borg anthem buffs itself and wide artifact boards; discard-removal mode prevents a dead draw when colors or board are awkward.

name: Lore, Positronic Provocateur
rationale: Hybrid artifact body either filters two cards or pushes an attacker through; modal ETB and artifact status make it easy to fit into several engines.

name: L'Rell, Fierce Visionary
rationale: Three-mana defensive body creates a temporary Klingon attacker every combat, including entry turn; sacrifice synergies turn those tokens into lasting value.

name: Mirror Universe Intrusion
rationale: Three-mana opposing-creature copy with menace scales with the best opposing threat; explicit kicker cost is six additional mana despite a conflicting reminder parenthesis.

name: Nog, Ambitious Cadet
rationale: Cheap menace threat becomes 3/4 for one mana, surveils when tapped and later replays graveyard lands; upgrades are permanent and can be paid off curve.

name: Phlox, Unorthodox Doctor
rationale: Trampling body turns countered creatures' combat damage into cards; needs counters on attackers and can draw multiple cards from a wide successful attack.

name: Sarek, Federation Ambassador
rationale: Five types for one card is plausible with diverse species and jobs; three-color 0/5 and a board-dependent draw threshold make unsupported hands awkward.

name: Seven of Nine
rationale: Four-mana 2/4 draws for every dilemma, including repeatable attack abilities and modal ETBs; substantial enabler density makes this a true archetype engine.
adjustment_reason: UB has repeatable dilemmas, modal creatures, cheap modal spells and modal lands; raw text models cannot learn a new mechanic's precise enabler density.

name: Spock, Always Your Friend
rationale: Two-mana body digs four for a noncreature nonland spell; spell-heavy UR often replaces it, but the selection can miss in creature-heavy builds.

name: The Traveler
rationale: Two-mana reach vigilance body starts at modest power and scales with distinct lands; three toughness stays fixed and two colors are required early.

name: Vash, Freelance Archaeologist
rationale: Durable three-mana body surveils each upkeep and draws once per turn from graveyard departures; beam and several common graveyard activations supply fuel.

name: Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior
rationale: Hybrid one-power creature can grow by tapping spare artifacts or summoning-sick bodies; eight-power attacks double its power but setup taps compete with combat and station.

name: Year of Hell
rationale: Symmetrical cards and damage usually leave you down the Saga card without affecting the board; direct draw-growth synergies rarely compensate reliably.

name: Zero, Incorporeal Sensate
rationale: Hybrid lifelink body taxes a chosen opposing hand card by two mana; disruption is temporary rather than permanent exile, but helps protect tempo.

name: Class-F Shuttlecraft
rationale: Three-mana any-color rock later becomes a flying vigilant blocker; six station counters require creatures, so the mana function is the dependable floor.

name: Combadge
rationale: Two Equipment copies need seven total mana to equip two creatures before unblockability works; lacks a stat boost and is slow when behind.

name: Crystalline Entity
rationale: Eight-mana flying 7/7 selectively sweeps nonartifact creatures when cast; strong payoff, but artifact-heavy opposing boards reduce the sweep and early copies are stranded.

name: Cybernetic Specialist
rationale: Colorless two-drop filters on entry and supports artifact boards; bottom-of-library activation triggers graveyard engines but is otherwise slow card recycling.

name: Deep Space 9
rationale: Nine-mana entry can immediately add several permanents and repeats each upkeep; mana cost is extreme and lands or dormant ships do not always stabilize at once.

name: Engineered Explosives
rationale: Flexible sunburst sweeper can clear token swarms or a chosen low mana-value band; color access limits the maximum, and the effect is symmetrical.

name: The Holodeck
rationale: Seven-mana artifact requires further mana to replay one permanent each turn; sideboard access helps selection but it usually lacks an immediate stabilizing play.

name: Isolinear Processor
rationale: Two-mana artifact ramp is restricted to artifacts and their abilities; looting is useful later and helps noncreature engines, but does not generate extra cards.

name: Replicator
rationale: Food provides an initial token and repeatable copying grows a board with Borg, Officers or Illusions; copying Food alone is not fast board development.

name: Sickbay
rationale: Five-mana artifact can put its first counter on a creature immediately; lifegain and later entries improve the rate, but it needs a surviving creature and time.

name: Tea, Earl Grey, Hot
rationale: Replaces itself on entry and leaves artifact fodder or a modal sacrifice activation; especially useful with dilemma payoffs and cheap artifact sacrifice.

name: Tricorder
rationale: Cheap Equipment improves both stats and attack selection with low equip cost; surplus copies and lack of bodies reduce standalone value.

name: Type-2 Phaser
rationale: Two-mana stun buys tempo and leaves a power Equipment, but equip three is costly and does not improve toughness.

name: U.S.S. Cerritos, Following Up
rationale: Two Officer bodies are immediate material and help charge the later 4/4 flyer; five mana and station six still require supporting creatures.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class
rationale: Charging generates immediate impulse access once each turn and a 4/5 flying vigilant body at seven; early triggers can be wasted if no mana or land play remains.
adjustment_reason: Repeated incremental charging can keep producing card access even after the ship becomes a creature; this engine need not stop at seven counters.

name: Warp Core
rationale: Finds a basic without ramping, then supplies recurring charge counters; enables ships without creature taps but costs mana and adds little without one.

name: Andoria
rationale: UR fixing plus life, Planet subtype and another unique name; tapped entry is a real tempo cost but supports several set mechanics.

name: Artificial Anomaly
rationale: Colorless source costs early color consistency; late drain and a replacement Planet add reach, life and a landfall trigger.

name: Bajor
rationale: RW dual supplies life and unique-land support; eight-power aggressive decks feel the tapped-entry cost more than slower decks.

name: Blood Crypt
rationale: BR dual can enter untapped for life; helps double-pip costs and supplies a unique name, but lacks Planet subtype or intrinsic card advantage.

name: Breeding Pool
rationale: GU dual can enter untapped when tempo matters and contributes a new name; not itself a Planet for tutoring.

name: Cardassia Prime
rationale: WB fixing supports Borg decks while lifegain and Planet name help broader synergies; enters tapped.

name: Earth, Sector 001
rationale: GU lifegain Planet fixes landfall and unique-name decks; tapped entry is balanced by relevant subtype and life triggers.

name: Federation Outpost
rationale: Often untapped after turn two and gives a modal life-or-surveil ETB, supporting dilemma triggers at almost no late-game cost.

name: Ferenginar
rationale: BG lifegain Planet fixes graveyard-value decks and adds a distinct name; tapped entry is its main cost.

name: Gaseous Anomaly
rationale: Colorless source weakens early colored casting; late draw two while replacing the land is meaningful flood protection and adds landfall.

name: Godless Shrine
rationale: WB shock dual improves mana without mandatory tapped entry; distinct-name value remains despite no Planet subtype.

name: Hallowed Fountain
rationale: WU shock dual supports early gold creatures and double-white or double-blue spells; life payment and lack of Planet subtype are modest costs.

name: Ni'Var Science Academy
rationale: Usually untapped from land three onward; modal surveil or temporary flying helps dilemmas, card quality and finishing attacks.

name: Orion
rationale: RG lifegain Planet supports repeated landfall and land-name discounts while fixing colors; tapped entry can interrupt aggressive curves.

name: Overgrown Tomb
rationale: BG shock dual supports splashes and gold engines with an untapped option; no entry card advantage or Planet subtype.

name: Q Continuum
rationale: Modal surveil is the default value and temporary vigilance/pump can affect combat; most late copies enter untapped and trigger dilemma payoffs.

name: Qo'noS
rationale: BR lifegain Planet fixes sacrifice decks and contributes a different name; life buys time but tapped entry slows pressure.

name: Quark's Bar
rationale: Modal land offers surveil or a final point of damage after turn two, while providing red mana without most late-game tempo loss.

name: Risa
rationale: GW lifegain Planet supports counter and lifegain creatures as well as land-name mechanics; tapped entry affects early development.

name: Romulus
rationale: UB lifegain Planet fixes dilemma decks and supports names-based effects; life and Planet subtype are small additional benefits.

name: Sacred Foundry
rationale: RW shock dual gives an untapped option important for aggressive curves; new land name supports broader set effects.

name: Spatial Anomaly
rationale: Colorless early source becomes late two-damage removal with a replacement Planet; targets small engines but activation costs six mana including this land.

name: Starfleet Academy
rationale: Colorless source has little payoff until federation counts enough types to exceed the five-mana activation plus tapped land; Borg decks reduce the count further.

name: Steam Vents
rationale: UR shock dual supports repeated spell turns with an untapped option and adds a distinct land name.

name: Stomping Ground
rationale: RG shock dual improves early creature curves and multi-spell turns; later unique-name support is useful but it cannot be found as a Planet.

name: Subspace Anomaly
rationale: Colorless early source converts to two Officers and a replacement Planet late; supports tokens, landfall, sacrifice and eight-power boards.

name: Temple Garden
rationale: GW shock dual fixes counter decks and can preserve early tempo; lacks the lifegain and tutorability of a Planet.

name: Temporal Anomaly
rationale: Colorless source later selects a permanent, fills the graveyard and replaces itself with a Planet; strong interaction with graveyard-departure and landfall engines.

name: Unexplored Territory
rationale: Untapped colorless initially, but fixing costs one mana plus tapping and sacrificing it; useful unique-name transition and landfall at a tempo cost.

name: The Unicomplex
rationale: Modal surveil is dependable, while putting a bomb creature back on top can dominate a late game; usually untapped after the first two land drops.

name: Vulcan
rationale: WU lifegain Planet fixes ship decks and supplies a tutor target and distinct name; tapping on entry is the main drawback.

name: Watery Grave
rationale: UB shock dual helps cast gold dilemma engines on time and can enter untapped; contributes a new name but no Planet subtype.

name: Plains
rationale: Basic white source; GIH primarily reflects white deck strength and land-draw selection rather than an intrinsic spell-like power rating.

name: Island
rationale: Basic blue source; forecast from historical basic-land behavior and predicted blue deck strength.

name: Swamp
rationale: Basic black source; forecast from historical basic-land behavior and predicted black deck strength.

name: Mountain
rationale: Basic red source; forecast from historical basic-land behavior and predicted red deck strength.

name: Forest
rationale: Basic green source; forecast from historical basic-land behavior and predicted green deck strength.
